The all-on-six implant is a type of dental implant that replaces the entire dental arch. Instead of making individual implants like classical implant types, they are fixed to the jawbone with six implant screws. What makes All on Six implant treatment different from classical implant treatments is not the number of implants, but the feature of the implant-supported prosthesis. The implant-supported prosthesis is placed on the implants by screwing them with spacers called multiunit.
What is the All On Six Implant Technique?

The all-on-six implant technique is performed much faster than classical dental implants. In classical implant treatments, there is a 3-month waiting period after the implant is placed in the jawbone. In the all-on-six implant technique, temporary fixed teeth are placed on the implants as soon as they are placed.

In the all-on-six implant treatment, a titanium screw is placed into the jawbone. Titanium screws are positioned at almost equal distances. Thus, they offer the strength that the jaw needs. Crown parts are produced from porcelain or zirconium.

All-on-six implant is a type of implant-supported dentures. While in classical treatments one implant is planned for each missing tooth, in this technique six implants are applied per jaw. The all-on-six implant technique is based on getting maximum efficiency from the prosthesis by providing extra support.
Who Can Have All-On-Six Implants?

The all on six implant technique is for those who want to have an entire dental arch implanted. It is a more cost-effective solution to replace the missing natural teeth. It offers a better appearance compared to denture teeth. They are also more comfortable due to their extra functionality.

The six implants used in the all-on-six implant technique give extra strength to the jaw. Bone loss that may occur due to missing teeth can be prevented. They are much more reliable for those looking for a long-term solution. The difference with all-on-four is that it gives extra strength to the jaw structure.

The situation of each person who wants to have an implant is different. If you want to have an all-on-six implant, your oral health and general health must be in good condition. Your dentist decides whether you are suitable for treatment by looking at images such as three-dimensional tomography.

These risks do not originate from the country where the treatment is performed. There are possible risks after every surgical procedure. Infection: If you ignore your dentist’s recommendations after treatment, you run the risk of infection. Infection causes implant treatment to fail. For this reason, you should follow your dentist’s recommendations.
Nerve Damage: If your dentist damages the nerves while placing the implant, you will experience some negative effects. If the nerves in the jaw are damaged, your lips and cheeks may become numb.

Sinus Complication: The sinus cavity, which is an anatomical space, is important for implant treatments. In patients who remain toothless for a long time, the sinus cavity sags downwards and causes bone resorption. This complication may also occur during All-on-six implant treatment.

In general, the success rate of implant treatments is very high. If your dentist is experienced, you will not have any problems. However, if you see an inexperienced dentist to reduce the cost of treatment, you may face the risk of complications.

Everything You Need to Know About Tooth Tartar

Tooth tartar, or calculus with its medical name, is one of the mouth problems that many people experience. Having information about tooth tartar and getting rid of tooth tartar with the most accurate medical interventions in the early period is much more important and necessary than many people assume. Let’s explore everything you need to know about tooth tartar and the important details regarding the subject.
What is Tooth Tartar?

Tooth tartar is the stony structure formed as a result of the bacterial plaques accumulating on the tooth surfaces hardening by interacting with the mineral in the content of the saliva. Plaques accumulating on the tooth surface can turn into tooth tartar within very short periods like 20 – 24 hours due to constant interaction with saliva. tooth tartar, which has both live and dead bacteria in its content, although it causes superficial problems like bad breath or the disruption of aesthetic appearance in the first stage, can put dental health and even general health status at risk in the long term.
Why Does Tooth Tartar Occur?

There are many different situations that can be listed among the reasons for the formation of tooth tartar. Important situations triggering the formation of tooth tartar can be categorized as follows:
Incorrect Oral Care Routines

Although many people think that tooth tartar forms only due to health problems, the situation is actually not like this. Oral care should be done in a quite delicate and regular way. Even though a large part of people sees oral and dental care as just consisting of brushing teeth, actually, the right oral and dental care routine must include both regular and correct tooth brushing and flossing. Individuals fulfilling their oral and dental care routines only by brushing their teeth in a superficial format can lead to the formation of tooth tartar as it causes plaques to remain.
Saliva Structure Containing Minerals at a High Rate

Tooth tartar forms as a result of plaques interacting with the minerals found in the saliva content. Because of this, individuals whose saliva structure is very rich in terms of minerals like calcium and phosphate are genetically more prone to tooth tartar formation. This proneness, especially when combined with factors triggering tooth tartar formation like applying incorrect oral care routines, can cause the individual to frequently face tooth tartar at certain intervals despite having a tooth tartar removal.
Having a Sugar-Heavy Diet

Having a sugar-heavy diet can indirectly lead to tooth tartar formation because it ensures the nourishment and rapid reproduction of bacteria in the mouth. Especially individuals who do not pay attention to teeth cleaning even though they constantly have a carbohydrate and sugar-heavy diet can frequently face tooth tartar.
Use of Tobacco Products

The use of tobacco products can also indirectly cause tooth tartar formation. Individuals using tobacco products like cigarettes witness their saliva secretions decreasing due to this use. The decrease of saliva secretion can cause a part of the saliva secretion, which has a protection and cleaning effect on the teeth albeit minimally, to be lost, and because of this, it can cause the plaque layers on the teeth to petrify.
Tooth Alignment Not Allowing Deep Teeth Cleaning

Tooth alignment not allowing deep teeth cleaning is one of the main situations causing tooth tartar formation. Many people whose teeth are aligned in a crooked way have difficulty on the subject of completely cleaning their tooth surfaces and between them due to this situation. Not being able to completely clean the tooth surfaces and between them can cause tooth tartar to form as it is triggering on the subject of bacteria reproduction and plaque accumulation.
How to Remove Tooth Tartar?
tartar tooth removal is an important medical intervention that must be performed by passing through a few steps. The stages of tartar tooth removal can be handled under several headings.
Comprehensive Examination

To remove tooth tartar, first of all, it is necessary to examine the patient comprehensively. This comprehensive examination, which helps to have information about the individual’s general oral health and the situations caused by the tooth tartar problem, helps an appropriate treatment planning to be made for the person by obtaining clear data about measurements like tooth tartar pocket depths, if any.
Breaking and Cleaning tooth tartar with Ultrasonic Devices

Breaking and cleaning tooth tartar with ultrasonic devices comes at the beginning of the main stages of tooth tartar removal. In order to get rid of tooth tartar in the healthiest way, it is necessary to break and shatter the tooth tartar with the ultrasonic vibration effect. The tooth tartar that is broken, shattered, and subsequently, the tartar that broke off the tooth is removed from the mouth without damaging the tooth enamel thanks to the water and cooling mechanisms used in ultrasonic devices.
Performing Fine Cleaning with a Curette

The stage of performing fine cleaning with a curette, which is one of the final stages of the tartar tooth removal procedure, is a quite important stage. The curette is one of the medical materials referred to as a dental tooth scaler tartar remover among the public, and it especially helps to scrape the tooth tartar that creates pockets in the gum and cannot be cleaned with ultrasonic devices.
Polishing Procedure

In the polishing stage, which is the final stage of tooth tartar removal, a medical procedure is applied to the teeth with a special polish material. Thanks to this procedure, the surfaces that have become rough and excessively matte after the tooth tartar removal are ensured to be both slippery and smooth. The polishing procedure is a quite important and necessary procedure in terms of tooth tartar not forming again in the near future.
Can Tartar Cause Tooth Decay?

Although many people confuse tooth tartar, especially the dark-colored ones, with tooth decays, actually tooth tartar and decay are things different from each other. However, situations like tooth tartar creating a ground for the reproduction of bacteria causing acid production on the tooth and making oral care routines like brushing teeth difficult can cause tooth tartar to lead to big decays in advancing terms.
Can You Remove Tooth Tartar at Home?

You should not perform tooth tartar removal at home. Although many people think they can perform tooth tartar removal at home by buying materials called dental tooth scaler tartar remover sold in mediums like online shopping sites, the situation is actually not like this. It is almost impossible to do the tooth tartar removal at home procedure correctly and completely.

dental tooth scaler tartar removers that can be used at home are generally materials that do not have the necessary features like cooling the tooth by squirting water; because of this, attempting tooth tartar removal at home can lead to severe consequences, including tooth loss while trying to get rid of tooth tartar occurring. On the other hand, since tartar tooth removal is a procedure that must be done delicately by expert dentists, incorrect interventions individuals will do to themselves at home can endanger their general health status as well.
What Happens if tooth tartar is Not Cleaned?
Not cleaning tooth tartar can create a ground for many negative situations to occur. Situations that can be experienced if tartar tooth removal is neglected can be explained under several headings.
Chronic Bad Breath

The formation of chronic bad breath comes at the beginning of the situations that will be experienced if tartar tooth removal is neglected. tooth tartar are bacteria nests, and because of this, there is sulfur production in the regions where tooth tartar is located. These volatile sulfur compounds cause the formation of a smell in the mouth that does not pass and becomes quite disturbing. The bad breath occurring due to tooth tartar becomes chronic as long as you do not get rid of tooth tartar.
Formation of an Unesthetic Appearance

Not cleaning tooth tartar can cause the formation of an unesthetic appearance. Even individuals who have quite white and properly aligned healthy teeth under normal conditions can cause their smile appearance to be disrupted due to tooth tartar because tooth tartar adds a yellowish color to the teeth in the first stage and can cause an appearance as if the teeth are decayed and completely blackened in the subsequent stages.
Occurrence of Gum Diseases

Contrary to what is assumed, tooth tartar accumulates not only on tooth surfaces and between them but also between the tooth and the gum. This accumulation leads to the formation of periodontal pockets in the gums. These periodontal pockets in question, by pushing the gum in a downward direction, can cause gum recession in the first stage and the occurrence of different gum diseases along with it. The loss of gum health can damage both oral health and general health status in the long term.
Tooth Losses

Many individuals who do not have a tooth tartar removal despite needing it for long years can witness their teeth, which are not even decayed, shaking and falling out. The main reason for this situation is that tooth tartar causes great damages to the jawbone and the tissues between the tooth in the long term, leading to the teeth shaking and ultimately falling out.
Increase in Inflammation Throughout the Body

Although it sounds interesting, tooth tartar can cause an increase in inflammation throughout the body and even the damage of various organs of the body. The opening of gum pockets, the mixing of harmful bacteria accumulating in the region into the blood, and the immune system constantly having to fight an infection; can cause an increase in inflammation throughout the body and the general health status progressing in a bad direction.
What Does It Mean When Tartar falling off on Its Own?

Tartar falling off on its own generally points out that the time to have a tooth tartar removal has already come. Although many people think that the teeth are healthily getting rid of tooth tartar and assume this situation is a positive development when they see the tartar chipped off tooth, the situation is actually not like this. In addition to this, tartar falling off on its own is generally a tooth tartar piece breaking off from areas like tooth surfaces, and it is not quite possible for the tooth tartar in the gum pockets to fall off on its own. Due to all these, if your tooth tartar is falling off on its own, you should urgently consult a dentist to have a tooth tartar removal.

What to Expect After Wisdom Tooth Extraction: A Complete Recovery Guide

Some situations and various factors that occur after wisdom tooth extraction cause individuals to be curious about some subjects. Let’s explore the detailed and scientific answers to the questions that come to mind after wisdom tooth extraction, the important details regarding the subject, and the important information that needs to be known regarding the healing process.
What to Eat After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

After wisdom tooth extraction, first of all, you need to get the doctor’s approval regarding nutrition and have waited long enough. After all these, you need to consume things that are not very hot, very cold, very hard, or grainy. For example, while beverages like hot soup lead to the expansion of the vessels, causing bleeding, grainy and very hard foods can cause destruction in the operation area where the wisdom teeth were extracted. Therefore, you need to consume foods like mashed banana, warm soup, or various fruit purees.
When is the Gauze Removed After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

When the gauze will be removed after wisdom tooth extraction can show variance depending on the situation. However, in general, it is recommended to wait at least 45 – 50 minutes for the gauze to be removed after wisdom tooth extraction. This period is an important and necessary time for a blood clot to form in the operation areas where the tooth extraction was performed and cavities were formed. Stopping biting the gauze or removing the gauze immediately after the tooth extraction or without waiting for at least 45 minutes to pass can mean facing an intense bleeding that endangers the healing process.
When Can I Drink Alcohol After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

It is necessary to wait at least 2 – 3 days to drink alcohol after wisdom tooth extraction. The first 24 – 48 hour period after the tooth extraction is the time frame where there is a risk of bleeding and the early healing period of the wound takes place. Drinking alcohol in this time frame means causing bleeding and sabotaging the healing. On the other hand, many patients have to use antibiotic medication against the risk of infection after wisdom tooth extraction. Drinking alcohol during the period when antibiotic medication is used is a quite risky situation. Because of this, it is necessary to wait at least 2 – 3 days to drink alcohol after wisdom tooth extraction and, if antibiotic use is in question, to wait until the medication use is finished.
When Can I Smoke After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

It is necessary to wait for at least 36 hours, that is, for three days, to smoke after wisdom tooth extraction. Cigarette use causes negative pressure in the mouth and makes healing difficult in various ways. Therefore, it is necessary to stay completely away from cigarettes in the first 3 days after wisdom tooth extraction. Otherwise, you may face bleeding and infections.
Why Do My Other Teeth Ache After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

The aching of other teeth after wisdom tooth extraction actually generally stems not from extreme situations like the failure of the tooth extraction but from situations considered natural and normal. The nerves to which the wisdom teeth are connected are also connected to other teeth, and because of this, many people feel as if their other teeth are also aching after the tooth extraction. On the other hand, situations like the wisdom teeth being extracted after applying pressure to the surrounding teeth for a long time can also cause sensitivity, leading you to feel as if your other teeth are aching. However, these are generally situations considered normal and pass on their own within a few days.
When Can I Drink Carbonated Beverages After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

It is necessary to wait for at least 4 – 5 days to consume carbonated beverages after wisdom tooth extraction. There is carbonic acid in carbonated beverages, and this substance can damage the area that has been irritated by the tooth extraction and has become open to destruction. On the other hand, the high sugar found in carbonated beverages can also cause destruction in the region and the blood clot to dislodge. Because of all these, it is necessary to wait for at least 4 – 5 days and, if possible, until healing completely occurs to drink carbonated beverages after wisdom tooth extraction.
Is Cheek Swelling and Bruising Normal After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

Although cheek swelling and bruising after wisdom tooth extraction seems like a quite worrying situation, it is actually normal. The majority of patients who have their wisdom teeth extracted witness that a swelling, that is, an edema, occurs in their cheeks, even if minimally, after the extraction procedure. Especially patients who have their fully impacted wisdom teeth extracted and whose tooth extraction procedures were quite difficult due to the teeth being impacted may face an intense edema and bruising. The edema and bruising in question stem from fluid accumulation in the region as a part of healing and generally begin to decrease within a few days.
When Are Teeth Brushed After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

It is necessary to wait at least 24 hours for the teeth to be brushed after wisdom tooth extraction. In this 24-hour period, it is recommended not only that the area where the wisdom teeth were formerly located but also the other teeth are not brushed, and no foreign substance, including toothpaste, is introduced into the mouth. However, after the 24-hour period is passed, the operation area where the wisdom teeth were formerly located cannot be brushed, but the other teeth can be brushed. While brushing the other teeth, it is necessary to avoid situations like fast and hard brushing movements and performing a hard swishing movement over the operation area while spitting out the toothpaste.
Why is Spitting and Rinsing the Mouth Forbidden After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

The main reason why spitting and rinsing the mouth are forbidden after wisdom tooth extraction is that a pressure occurs in the mouth during the mouth rinsing movement. This pressure causes the blood clot to separate from the area where the wisdom teeth were extracted and covered with a blood clot, and to move away from the mouth with spitting. The dislodgment of the blood clot and its removal from the mouth also causes bleeding to occur in the area, and as a result of losing the blood clot that will ensure the completion of healing, you may have to go through a very difficult and dangerous healing period.
The Resting Position That Accelerates the Healing Process After Wisdom Tooth Extraction

The resting position that accelerates the healing process after wisdom tooth extraction is the supine sleeping position where the head is supported with a very high pillow or two standard pillows. Since the head region remains elevated in this position, the blood pressure going to the head region drops, and this drop in pressure is a preventive measure for many different situations, from the occurrence of bleeding risk in the region to the increase of edema formation. In addition to all these, this resting position can also be supported with neck support pillows.
Situations Indicating You Should Consult Your Dentist After Wisdom Tooth Extraction

Intense bleeding that continues for a very long time comes at the beginning of the situations indicating you need to consult your dentist after wisdom tooth extraction. Bleeding after tooth extraction and slight blood coming for a few days are considered normal, but if this bleeding is very intense and continues for long periods, something might be going wrong. In addition to this, your fever rising and a purulent discharge coming from the region are also among the situations indicating you should consult your dentist after wisdom tooth extraction.
When Can I Use a Straw After Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

It is necessary to wait for at least a week or 10 days to use a straw after wisdom tooth extraction. Although many people think that using a straw after tooth extraction is much safer than drinking liquids directly from a glass, the situation is not actually like this. Straw use is quite dangerous because it creates pressure in the mouth, which can cause the blood clot to come out of the extraction area. Therefore, you need to avoid using a straw for at least 1 week or 10 days after your tooth extraction procedure.

Is Wisdom Tooth Extraction Necessary?

There are some situations where wisdom tooth extraction is necessary. However, contrary to what is believed, not every individual needs their wisdom teeth to be extracted. Some individuals can use their wisdom teeth in a healthy way or, even if rarely, since some individuals’ wisdom teeth do not exist, their need for wisdom tooth extraction automatically disappears. In summary, the extraction of wisdom teeth is not necessary in every patient and in every situation.

The situations where the extraction of wisdom teeth is necessary are primarily the situations where wisdom teeth remain fully impacted or semi-impacted. Because wisdom teeth remaining fully or semi-impacted can cause the disruption of tooth alignment by applying pressure to other teeth located in the surroundings, the formation of cysts in the jawbone, the occurrence of gingival inflammations, and severe pains, the removal of these teeth is quite important and necessary. Not having the wisdom teeth extracted that are necessary to be extracted can cause not only the wisdom teeth to be damaged in the long term but also the general oral and dental health to be disrupted.
Things to Do Before Wisdom Tooth Extraction
It is necessary to do some important things before wisdom tooth extraction. The important things that need to be done can be handled under several headings.
1. Finding a Reliable Healthcare Institution

As in every kind of medical intervention, the first and most important thing that needs to be done before wisdom tooth extraction is to find a reliable healthcare institution. A reliable healthcare institution takes actions that will prevent you from worrying about subjects like sterilization during tooth extraction procedures. On the other hand, reliable healthcare institutions like Dentaliva take precautions in the name of preventing situations such as the damaging of the nerves in the region from occurring during such procedures by performing the tooth extraction procedures with dentists who are experts in their fields. Due to all these, it is necessary to find a reliable healthcare institution before wisdom tooth extraction.
2. Not Consuming Alcohol and Cigarettes for At Least 24 – 48 Hours

You need to take care not to consume cigarettes and alcohol for at least 24 – 48 hours before wisdom tooth extraction. Consuming alcohol before a complicated medical intervention like a wisdom tooth extraction procedure means dropping the blood clot formation time and the quality of this clot after tooth extraction. Smoking cigarettes, on the other hand, is quite harmful because it shrinks the vessels and negatively affects the transportation of oxygen to the tissues. Due to all these, try to stay away from cigarettes and alcohol for at least 1 – 2 days before having your wisdom teeth extracted.
3. Taking a Break from Blood Thinner Medication Usage by Getting Doctor Approval

Another thing that needs to be done before wisdom tooth extraction is to take a break from blood thinner medication usage. Blood thinner medications are quite important and necessary medications for some individuals with coagulation problems. However, the usage of these medications before medical procedures where blood is needed to clot quickly and healthily, like a wisdom tooth extraction procedure, can put the procedure process and the healing process at risk. Because of this, you must stop using blood thinner medication before tooth extraction. However, you must also not forget that you need to consult your doctor while taking a break from blood thinner medication usage. Otherwise, situations like you not using blood thinners for periods long enough to experience coagulation problems can occur.
4. Paying Attention to General Oral and Dental Health

Many people think that situations like these teeth decaying or holding dental calculus before having their wisdom teeth extracted are unimportant. However, the situation is not actually like this. Even if the wisdom teeth will be extracted, it is necessary to be protected from health problems like tooth decays and dental calculi by paying attention to general oral and dental health because the occurrence of problems like infection in the operation region in question can cause the procedure not to be able to be done or to be done with a high risk rate. Because of this, before wisdom tooth extraction, you need to deeply clean all of your teeth, including the region where your wisdom teeth are located, with materials like a toothbrush and dental floss.
Can I Eat Before a Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

You need to not eat before wisdom tooth extraction. The last meal before wisdom tooth extraction should not be eaten in the 3 – 4 hours before the procedure. It is necessary to not eat for at least 3 – 4 hours before the wisdom tooth extraction procedures that will be performed under local anesthesia. Before the tooth extraction procedures that will be performed under general anesthesia, on the other hand, it is necessary to not eat anything and not drink anything, including water, for at least 8 hours. Otherwise, the operation and anesthesia process can get under risk.
Can Wisdom Tooth Extraction Be Done Under General Anesthesia?

Wisdom tooth extraction can be done under general anesthesia. before wisdom tooth extraction, some patients can request the application of general anesthesia because they feel very worried about the procedure and are very afraid of suffering pain. On the other hand, patients whose wisdom teeth are very strong or who will not be able to remain stable throughout the operation due to the gag reflex may also need to benefit from general anesthesia. In such situations, by keeping factors like the individual’s general health status in view, it can be decided to do tooth extraction with general anesthesia application.

Especially equipped healthcare institutions like Dentaliva, because they also meet the requirements on the subject of general anesthesia, can ensure the successful completion of tooth extraction procedures done under general anesthesia with anesthesia specialists who are experts in their fields.
Is a Blood Test Done Before Wisdom Tooth Extraction?

Factors That Can Damage Braces

Braces are the most common orthodontic treatment to straighten teeth and bite properly. It is also important for your teeth to look straight for a healthy-looking smile. This is also possible with the help of braces. Because crooked teeth can prevent a person from smiling in social life and from showing his teeth. However, this treatment includes some factors that patients should pay attention to. Being aware of these factors that can damage braces is essential to ensure successful and effective treatment. Braces are an effective orthodontic treatment method used to solve dental problems that require straightening. However, braces can be damaged if proper care and attention is not given. Factors that damage brackets and wires are as follows. Knowing these situations at the beginning of the treatment helps prevent damage to the braces.
Hard and Sticky Foods

Hard and sticky foods can damage your braces. Snacks such as chips, hard candies, gum and nuts can damage the wires. Such foods can cause the wires to break or split. Therefore, such foods should be avoided during the treatment period to protect your teeth and braces. Harmful effects of hard foods on braces may be as follows:
Hard foods can cause braces to break. This may prolong the treatment process and cause extra costs.

Sticky and hard foods may cause the position of the wires to change. In other words, the adjustment made by the orthodontist on the braces may be disrupted. This may prolong the treatment process and prevent successful results.
Hard foods can cause aches and pains. This may cause patients to feel uncomfortable and avoid eating.
Chewing gum can cause your braces to become misaligned.
These foods may contain sugar and acid, which can lead to tooth decay. This can threaten dental health and make the treatment process more complicated.
Some precautions you can take to prevent hard foods from damaging your braces are:
Avoid hard foods or consume them in small food particles.
Make sure to eat soft and healthy foods after wearing your braces, so that you do not put too much pressure on your braces.
Clean braces regularly and follow your dentist’s recommended care instructions.
Poor Oral Hygiene

Braces are places where food particles and plaque build up easily. Poor oral hygiene can lead to tooth decay, gum problems, and stains on teeth and braces. It is necessary to ensure cleanliness between the wires by brushing your teeth, flossing and using mouthwash regularly.
Inadequate oral hygiene can have negative effects on braces and prolong the treatment process. Here is some information about how poor oral hygiene affects braces:

Plaque Buildup: Braces are designed to prevent the buildup of food particles and bacteria. However, inadequate oral hygiene may cause this accumulation to increase. Plaque accumulation can lead to tooth decay and gum problems.
Gum problems: Inadequate hygiene can lead to gum swelling, bleeding and gingivitis. This can cause discomfort and pain around the braces.
Stains and Color Changes: Inadequate oral hygiene can cause teeth staining and color changes. This can make it difficult to achieve the same color when the braces are removed.
Tooth Decay: Braces contain areas where food particles and plaque buildup can easily become trapped. Inadequate oral hygiene can cause tooth decay in these areas.
Prolongation of the Treatment Process: Problems arising from inadequate oral hygiene may prolong the treatment process. Straightening braces and achieving results may require more time and effort.

For the above reasons, it is extremely important to have a regular and effective oral hygiene routine after getting braces. Follow your dentist’s recommended brushing, flossing, and mouthwash instructions to clean the areas around your braces and keep your teeth in good condition. Additionally, regular dentist visits are important to check the health of your braces and the treatment process.
Teeth Grinding or Clenching

Braces can wear or break due to constant clenching or grinding of teeth. These habits can compromise the success of treatment and prolong treatment time. If there is a problem with the brackets or wires, it is important to consult an orthodontist immediately.
Loosening or Movement of Braces

Clenching the teeth may cause the braces to loosen or move. Braces are placed in a specific way to straighten teeth, and these positions must be maintained. Otherwise, it may cause the straightened teeth to return to their previous positions.
Braces Breakage

Clenching your teeth can cause braces to break. This means the cables may need to be replaced or repaired. This may prolong the treatment process and increase costs. You can contact us for a beautiful smile aesthetics.
Pain and Discomfort
Clenching teeth can cause pain and discomfort in the mouth and jaw area. This may cause the treatment process to be more uncomfortable and difficult.
Tooth Decay
Clenching teeth can cause teeth to rub against each other. This can cause tooth decay or cause this negative condition to progress because cleaning between the teeth becomes more difficult.
Pressure
Clenching your teeth puts extra pressure on the braces. This can cause the strings to be tighter on it.
Not Using Mouth Guard During Sports

If you are actively involved in sports and wear braces, it is important to wear a mouth guard. Impacts to the teeth during sports can damage the braces. Wearing a mouth guard helps protect your teeth and braces.
Going to Check-ups Irregularly:

You should visit the dentist regularly throughout the treatment process. The dentist can evaluate the condition of the wires, make adjustments and detect problems when necessary. Regular check-ups are the key to successful treatment.
Hurt of Brackets and Wires:

Brackets and wires can sometimes be accidentally injured or broken. Such situations can delay the straightening of the teeth and cause discomfort. In case of strains or fractures, you should see an orthodontist immediately.

In conclusion, braces are a very effective treatment method for solving dental problems. However, paying attention to factors that may damage braces ensures successful progress and outcome of the treatment. Oral hygiene, diet, sports activities and regular medical check-ups are important to protect braces. If any problems occur, it would be best to see an orthodontist.

Bleeding Gums: Causes & Treatment

Bleeding gums are a symptom of diseases that occur primarily in the gums. However, apart from gum diseases, the underlying cause may also be other health problems. Harsh tooth brushing, incorrect use of dental floss, and mistakes in using dentures can cause bleeding in the gums. In addition to routine daily problems, bleeding gums may also indicate chronic conditions such as diabetes, hemophilia, and low platelet count in the blood.

Gums or also known as gingiva; It is a mucosa tissue that surrounds the teeth and acts as a protective barrier. It helps grind food by settling firmly into the bone tissues it surrounds. It prevents food residues from passing into the periodontal areas. The color of the gums is coral pink in healthy individuals.

Gums have a tissue rich in blood vessels. If the vessels in the gum tissue are damaged due to internal and external factors, people experience bleeding gums. The most common cause of bleeding gums is excessive plaque accumulated in the gums. The sticky bacterial plaque called gingivitis that occurs after this accumulation causes inflammation in the gums. These plaques cause bleeding in the gums. Excessive plaque accumulation can lead to bleeding as well as a jaw bone condition called periodontitis. These disorders negatively affect people’s oral health. The treatment of this disorder, which negatively affects the person’s health and may have different sub-causes, should be started as soon as possible under the supervision of a dentist.
What are the Causes of Bleeding Gums?

The most important cause of gum bleeding is inadequate oral hygiene and gingivitis inflammation. Chronic diseases or vitamin deficiencies should be examined in case of constantly recurring gum bleeding. The most necessary thing to prevent bleeding gums is to learn the causes of this problem thoroughly.
Physical Trauma: Hard and shelly foods consumed by patients or external damage to the tooth structure may cause gum bleeding.
Intraoral Prosthesis: People using dentures or oral prostheses that do not fit their mouth structure can damage teeth and gums and cause gum bleeding.
Pregnancy: Hormonal changes during pregnancy cause edema in the gums or excessive blood flow to the gum area. Pregnant women may experience bleeding gums due to these changes in hormones.
Chronic Diseases: Chronic diseases that damage the gums, such as diabetes, blood clotting problem (hemophilia), decrease in the number of platelets in the blood, can cause gum bleeding.

Vitamin deficiencies; Vitamins C and K are very important for the health of gum tissues. Vitamin C is indispensable for the connecting tissues surrounding the teeth and jaw bones. Vitamin C contributes to the development of tissues in the body and accelerates the healing of tissue wounds. Vitamin K deficiency causes problems in blood clotting, which can cause bleeding disorders. As a result of people taking insufficient vitamins C and K, their gums may be affected by vitamin deficiency. Therefore, foods rich in vitamins C and K should be consumed.

Bleeding gums while brushing teeth is the most common symptom experienced by people. When a person thinks that he or she is experiencing gum bleeding for no reason, there is actually an underlying reason. This may be due to harsh use of dental floss and toothbrush or bad nutrition habits.
Factors Related to Oral Hygiene
One of the frequently seen factors that causes bleeding gums is oral hygiene.

Gingivitis: It is the inflammation that occurs in the oral dental tissue. Inflammation of the gums is one of the most common causes of bleeding gums.
Smoking: The chemicals used in cigarette production damage the gum structure by damaging it. Damage to the gum can make the gum prone to bleeding.
Many different diseases can cause bleeding gums, not only oral hygiene habits or diseases caused by inflammation of the gums.
What are the symptoms of bleeding gums?

The most common symptom seen by people is blood on the gums during tooth brushing, on the toothbrush or in the water after rinsing the mouth. Additionally, tooth sensitivity is another symptom. Pain in the gums due to hot and cold sensitivity, pressure on the gums, turning of the gums from pink to red, swelling in the gums, and excessive pressure on the gums due to dental dentures are the main symptoms of gum bleeding.

Brush your teeth at least twice a day, in a way that does not damage the capillaries and tooth tissue.
You can keep your mouth hygienic by using dental floss and mouthwash solutions.

The vitamin content in the body is possible with a balanced diet. Therefore, for good oral and dental health, you should regularly consume foods rich in vitamins K and C. Also, drink plenty of water during the day to prevent inflammation of the gums that may occur due to dry mouth.
Stop smoking and alcohol. Because these bad habits damage the gum structure.
See your dentist regularly to have your dentures checked and smile aesthetics.
Is Bleeding Gums Risky?

While gum bleeding may start while brushing your teeth and stop within a few seconds, it may also be caused by inflammation. Since dental disorders can also lead to cardiac problems, gum health should be taken into consideration, especially in pregnant women.
